environment: Humpback whales delight crowds with record sightings on their spring migration past the Sunshine Coast
Community reforestation crews celebrate a major tree planting milestone in the Bunya Mountains
science: Queensland researchers report promising early results in growing heat tolerant coral to help shield the Great Barrier Reef
sports: Queensland swimmers and athletes post strong personal bests as the state gears up for the summer sporting season
stories.overview: Spring whale watching season peaks along the Queensland coast with record humpback numbers spotted from the shore

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer, and mate it is a ripper of a spring day out there. We've got whales putting on a show, scientists chasing coral breakthroughs and Queensland athletes smashing personal bests, so plenty to get through. And I'm Jamie, and honestly Alex I could watch whale videos all day, it never gets old. We've got a jam packed bulletin for you, environment, science, sports and of course Sam's going to sort out your weekend weather plans. Too right. Grab a cuppa, settle in, and let's get into the good stuff happening right across the sunshine state.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Let's kick off with something that always gets me, the humpbacks are cruising past the Sunshine Coast right now and spotters reckon the numbers this spring are some of the best they have seen in years. Whole families of whales, calves and all, putting on an absolute show for anyone with a decent set of binoculars. Yeah I love this one, it is basically nature's own parade happening right off our coast. And up in the Bunya Mountains, local volunteers have just hit a huge milestone with their reforestation project, getting a heap of native trees back into the ground after years of hard slog. It is proof that when a community rolls up its sleeves, real change happens, tree by tree and whale by whale. Two lovely reminders that Queensland's wild side is doing just fine.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Now onto the science desk, and this one is a beauty for reef lovers. Researchers here in Queensland are having genuine success growing coral that can handle warmer water, which is huge news for the long term health of the Great Barrier Reef. It is early days but the results so far are really encouraging, and it gives everyone a bit of hope that we can help the reef ride out tougher conditions. Coral that can take the heat, who would have thought. Exactly, it is that classic Aussie approach, see a problem, roll up the sleeves and get on with fixing it. Big tick for the boffins on this one.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex and Jamie, good on ya. Now looking at the rest of the week across the south east, we are in for classic spring conditions, plenty of sunshine, light winds and top temps sitting comfortably in the mid to high twenties across Brisbane, the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast. Mornings are still a bit crisp so keep a jumper handy for the school run, but by lunchtime it will be lovely, beach worthy weather if you can sneak away. There is a slight chance of an afternoon shower building later in the week as we edge closer to storm season, so nothing to worry about yet but it is worth keeping an eye on the sky. All in all, a top few days to get outdoors and enjoy that Queensland spring.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Right, let's talk sport, and it is a good news story for our young guns. Queensland swimmers and track athletes have been posting some cracking personal bests at recent meets, right on cue as everyone gears up for the big summer season ahead. I love seeing that, especially the younger athletes coming through, it shows the depth of talent we have got in this state. A few of them are ones to watch heading into the bigger meets later in the year, mark my words. Too right, keep an eye on those names because I reckon we will be hearing a lot more from them. Great effort all round from our Queensland athletes.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: Well that is the Bright Side wrapped up for today, whales, trees, coral and cracking sport, not a bad way to spend twenty minutes. Thanks for hanging out with us. It really was a good one today, I am still thinking about those whale numbers to be honest. Thanks to Sam for sorting our weather plans too, sounds like a beauty of a week ahead. Absolutely, get outside, soak up that spring sunshine and maybe keep an eye out for a fin or two if you are near the coast. We will be back tomorrow with more good news from right across Queensland and beyond. Until then, look after yourselves and each other. See ya then, this has been ParkSyde Bright Side, take care out there.
